subject: economics
title: Loss Aversion and Prospect Theory
welcome_lead: Losses hurt more than gains feel good - and choices reflect it.
meta_desc: A-Level Behavioural Economics: loss aversion and prospect theory.
final_note: Loss aversion roughly doubles the weight of losses vs equivalent gains.

walkthroughs.body_html: Prospect theory replaces classical expected utility. Choices are made relative to a reference point; the value function is concave for gains, convex for losses, and steeper for losses.
Once people own something - even a coffee mug given five minutes ago - they demand far more to part with it than they would have paid to buy it.
Free trials, free returns and loyalty schemes all exploit loss aversion and endowment effects. Cancelling a subscription feels like a loss, so most people stick.

mcqs.q: What does dependency theory argue about development?
options: Poorer 'periphery' countries are kept underdeveloped by their economic relationships with rich 'core' countries — through unequal trade, debt and historical colonialism. It challenges the view that integration with rich economies automatically helps.
Dependency theory is about households relying on benefits.
A public good is anything that's free.
Dependency theory means poor countries are simply lazy.

options: A public good is anything that's free.
Dependency theory is about households relying on benefits.

A public good is anything provided by the government.
